YAAKOV — CHAPTERS 26 THROUGH 35

YOVELIM — CHAPTER 26 Yitzhak Blesses Yaakov — Esav's Anger

1 In the seventh year of the week, Yitzhak called Esav, his elder son, saying that he was old, his sight was dim, and the day of his death was unknown.

2 He told Esav to take his hunting gear, go into the field, bring game, and prepare the food he loved so that he might bless him before he died.

3 Rivkah heard Yitzhak speaking to Esav.

4 Esav went out early to hunt and bring game to his father.

5 Rivkah called Yaakov and told him what she had heard: Yitzhak intended to eat Esav's food and bless him before YHWH.

6 She ordered Yaakov to obey her and bring two good young goats from the flock so she could prepare food for Yitzhak as he liked it.

7 Yaakov answered that Esav was hairy while he was smooth, and feared that his father would feel him and regard him as a deceiver.

8 He feared bringing a curse upon himself instead of a blessing.

9 Rivkah told him that the consequence would rest on her and again commanded him to obey.

10 Yaakov brought the animals, and Rivkah prepared the food in the manner Yitzhak loved.

11 She clothed Yaakov with Esav's best garments and covered his hands and the smooth part of his neck with the goatskins.

12 She placed the food and bread in Yaakov's hands and sent him to his father.

13 Yaakov entered and addressed Yitzhak as his father; Yitzhak asked which son had come.

14 Yaakov presented himself as Esav and said he had done as his father commanded, asking him to rise and eat so that he might bless him.

15 Yitzhak wondered how the game had been found so quickly, and Yaakov answered that YHWH had caused it to come before him.

16 Yitzhak asked Yaakov to come near so he could touch him and determine whether he was truly Esav.

17 Yaakov approached; Yitzhak felt him and said the voice was Yaakov's voice but the hands were Esav's hands.

18 He did not recognize him because the covered hands were hairy, and he prepared to bless him.

19 Yitzhak again asked whether he was truly Esav, and Yaakov answered that he was.

20 Yitzhak asked for the food, ate what Yaakov brought, and drank the wine brought to him.

21 Yitzhak told his son to come near and kiss him.

22 When Yaakov came near, Yitzhak smelled Esav's garments and blessed him, comparing his son's fragrance to a field blessed by YHWH.

23 He blessed him with heaven's dew, the richness of the earth, and abundance of grain and produce.

24 He declared that peoples would serve him, his brothers would bow before him, and the blessings given to Avraham and Yitzhak would pass to him and his descendants; those who cursed him would be cursed and those who blessed him blessed.

25 After Yitzhak finished the blessing, Yaakov left his presence.

26 Esav returned from hunting, prepared food, and brought it to his father, asking Yitzhak to eat and bless him.

27 Yitzhak asked who he was, and Esav identified himself as the firstborn.

28 Yitzhak was greatly shaken and asked who had brought him food before Esav arrived; he said he had eaten and blessed that son, and the blessing would stand.

29 When Esav heard this, he cried out bitterly and begged his father to bless him also.

30 Yitzhak said Esav's brother had come by cunning and had taken the blessing; Esav protested that Yaakov had now displaced him twice, first regarding the birthright and now the blessing.

31 Esav asked whether no blessing had been reserved for him; Yitzhak replied that he had already made Yaakov master over his brothers and sustained him with abundance.

32 Esav wept and pleaded that his father give him even one blessing.

33 Yitzhak answered that Esav's dwelling would be away from the earth's richest portion and from the dew above.

34 He said Esav would live by the sword and serve his brother, but when he grew strong he would shake the yoke from his neck.

35 Esav hated Yaakov because of the blessing and resolved that after the days of mourning for their father he would kill his brother.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No securely mapped Qumran Jubilees locus is asserted as a direct Hebrew control for this chapter in this reader.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The continuous chapter sequence and content are checked against James C. VanderKam, The Book of Jubilees: A Critical Text / Translation (CSCO 510–511, 1989), based on the critical Ethiopic tradition. This reader does not claim a new diplomatic transcription of every individual Geʽez codex; Qumran Hebrew is applied only at extant loci.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] MT Genesis 27:1-41 is the direct comparison for the firstborn-blessing episode. Jubilees retells the deception and blessing within its own characterization of Rivkah, Yaakov, Esav, and the birthright, so MT wording does not govern the Yovelim account.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Chapter 26 is the firstborn-blessing episode. Its correct placement is a major structural control because earlier ACR scaffolds displaced Lavan material into this chapter. Any recurrence of Lavan-household narrative here is evidence of misbinding, not a variant segmentation.

YOVELIM — CHAPTER 27 Yaakov Sent Away — The Bethel Dream and Vow

1 Rivkah learned in a dream of Esav's intention to kill Yaakov and summoned her younger son.

2 She warned that Esav sought vengeance against him.

3 She told Yaakov to flee to her brother Lavan in Haran until Esav's anger passed, promising to send for him afterward.

4 Yaakov said he was not afraid and would defend himself if Esav attacked.

5 Rivkah pleaded that she not lose both sons in one day.

6 Yaakov answered that Yitzhak was old and nearly blind; he would not abandon his father without being sent, lest Yitzhak be angered and curse him.

7 Rivkah said she would speak to Yitzhak so that Yitzhak himself would send Yaakov away.

8 She told Yitzhak that Esav's Hittite wives made her life bitter and that she could not bear for Yaakov to marry a woman of Kena'an.

9 Yitzhak called Yaakov, blessed him, and instructed him not to take a wife from the daughters of Kena'an.

10 He ordered him to go to the house of Betuel in Aram and take a wife from the daughters of Lavan, Rivkah's brother.

11 Yitzhak asked the Almighty Creator to bless, multiply, and establish Yaakov as a multitude and to give him the blessing of Avraham and the land promised to his descendants.

12 Yitzhak sent Yaakov away in peace to Lavan son of Betuel.

13 After Yaakov departed, Rivkah grieved and wept for her son.

14 Yitzhak comforted her, saying Yaakov was going in peace and would return in peace.

15 He said the Most High Creator would guard Yaakov from evil and would not abandon him.

16 Yitzhak declared that Yaakov's way would prosper until he returned safely.

17 He told Rivkah not to fear because Yaakov walked uprightly and faithfully.

18 Yitzhak comforted Rivkah concerning Yaakov and renewed the blessing over him.

19 Yaakov left Be'er Sheva for Haran and reached Luz, that is Bethel, at the beginning of the first month.

20 At sunset he stopped, took a stone for his head, and slept there alone.

21 In the night he saw a stairway standing on the earth and reaching heaven, with angels ascending and descending, and YHWH above it.

22 YHWH identified himself as the Creator of Avraham and Yitzhak and promised Yaakov the land on which he slept for himself and his descendants.

23 He promised that Yaakov's descendants would spread west, east, north, and south and that families of the earth would receive blessing through his seed.

24 YHWH promised to remain with him, protect him wherever he went, and return him to that land without abandoning the promise.

25 Yaakov awoke in awe and recognized the place as the house of YHWH and a gate of heaven.

26 In the morning he set up the stone as a pillar, poured oil upon it, and named the place Bethel, though it had formerly been called Luz.

27 Yaakov vowed that if YHWH guarded him, provided food and clothing, and returned him safely to his father's house, YHWH would be his Creator; the pillar would mark YHWH's house, and he would give a tenth of all he received.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Chapter 27 combines Yaakov's departure with the Bethel dream and vow. The Bethel material belongs here in the continuous Yovelim sequence; Lavan pursuit, Esav reconciliation, or wrestling material at this locus would signal contamination from later narrative units.

YOVELIM — CHAPTER 28 Yaakov with Lavan — Leah, Rachel, the Children, and Wealth

1 Yaakov continued eastward and came to Lavan, Rivkah's brother, and served him seven years for Rachel.

2 When the service was complete, Yaakov asked Lavan to give him the wife for whom he had served.

3 Lavan prepared a feast and gave Leah, his elder daughter, to Yaakov, with Zilpah as her servant; Yaakov did not realize the substitution until afterward.

4 Yaakov confronted Lavan for deceiving him and said that he had served for Rachel, not Leah.

5 Lavan replied that in his country the younger daughter was not given before the elder.

6 Lavan told Yaakov to complete Leah's bridal week and promised Rachel also in return for another seven years of service.

7 Yaakov accepted and completed Leah's week.

8 Lavan then gave Rachel to Yaakov and gave Bilhah as Rachel's servant.

9 Yaakov served another seven years for Rachel and loved Rachel more than Leah.

10 When YHWH saw that Leah was less loved, he opened her womb while Rachel remained without children.

11 Leah bore Reuven, and his birth was recorded in the chronology of the jubilee.

12 She next bore Shim'on.

13 Leah bore Levi, whose name marked attachment.

14 She bore Yehudah and gave thanks for the child.

15 Rachel became jealous because she had borne no children and asked Yaakov to give her children.

16 Yaakov answered that he was not the one who had withheld the fruit of her womb.

17 Rachel gave Bilhah to Yaakov so that she might receive children through her servant.

18 Bilhah bore Dan.

19 Bilhah bore Naftali.

20 Leah gave Zilpah to Yaakov when she had ceased bearing for a time.

21 Zilpah bore Gad.

22 Zilpah bore Asher.

23 Leah again conceived and bore Yissakhar.

24 Leah bore Zevulun.

25 Afterward Leah bore a daughter, Dinah.

26 YHWH remembered Rachel and opened her womb.

27 Rachel bore Yosef and asked that another son be added to her.

28 After Yosef's birth Yaakov told Lavan that he wished to return to his own land and household.

29 Lavan persuaded him to remain for wages, and Yaakov's flocks increased greatly through the arrangement between them.

30 Yaakov became very wealthy in livestock, servants, camels, and donkeys, while Lavan and his sons became resentful of his prosperity.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Chapter 28 is the Lavan-household chapter: marriages, children, and Yaakov's increase in wealth form its continuous narrative core. Material formerly displaced into Chapter 26 must remain bound here.

YOVELIM — CHAPTER 29 Departure from Lavan — Reconciliation with Esav

1 When Yaakov perceived Lavan's changed attitude, he resolved to leave with his household and possessions.

2 He gathered his wives, children, servants, and livestock and departed from Paddan-Aram without announcing his departure to Lavan.

3 Rachel took the household images belonging to her father.

4 Lavan learned that Yaakov had fled and pursued him.

5 He overtook Yaakov in the hill country of Gil'ad.

6 In a night vision YHWH warned Lavan not to threaten Yaakov or compel him to return.

7 Lavan challenged Yaakov for departing secretly and for taking his daughters away without farewell.

8 Yaakov answered that he feared Lavan might take Leah and Rachel from him by force.

9 Lavan searched for his household images but did not find them because Rachel had concealed them.

10 Yaakov rebuked Lavan and recounted the years of difficult service in which he had borne the losses of the flocks and the extremes of heat and cold.

11 Lavan and Yaakov made a covenant, raised a witness heap, and agreed not to cross it against one another for harm.

12 Lavan kissed and blessed his daughters and grandchildren and returned to his place.

13 Yaakov crossed the Yabboq, and Esav came to meet him; the brothers were reconciled, and Esav returned to Seir while Yaakov remained with his tents.

14 Yaakov crossed the Yarden and pastured his flocks through the regions east and west of it as he moved through Kena'an.

15 He sent provisions regularly to his father Yitzhak and his mother Rivkah from all his substance.

16 Yaakov built for himself a house and shelters for his livestock and continued supporting his parents.

17 Esav settled permanently in the hill country of Seir and separated his possessions from Yaakov's because the land could not sustain both households together.

18 Esav's descendants established themselves in Seir among the sons of Seir the Horite.

19 Yaakov remained in the land of his fathers' sojournings, maintaining his household and the obligations toward Yitzhak and Rivkah.

20 The separation of the brothers' territories was thus established, Esav in Seir and Yaakov in Kena'an.

This reader does not claim a new diplomatic transcription of every individual Geʽez codex; Qumran Hebrew is applied only at extant loci.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] MT Genesis 31-33 supplies the departure from Lavan and reconciliation with Esav. Jubilees heavily abbreviates both encounters and does not reproduce the MT wrestling episode of Genesis 32:25-33 as part of this chapter's sequence.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Chapter 29 carries the flight/reconciliation and family-support sequence into Esav's settlement. Its structure is significantly shorter than the full Genesis 31-33 complex, so missing biblical episodes should not be supplied unless Yovelim's own witnesses attest them.

YOVELIM — CHAPTER 30 Dinah — Shekhem — Intermarriage Law — Levi

1 Yaakov came peacefully to the region of Shekhem during the first year of the sixth week.

2 Dinah, Yaakov's twelve-year-old daughter, was taken by Shekhem son of Hamor the Hivite, who violated her.

3 Shekhem desired Dinah and asked his father and her brothers to obtain her as his wife.

4 Yaakov and his sons were enraged because of what had been done to Dinah.

5 Shim'on and Levi entered the city and killed the men responsible, acting in judgment for their sister's defilement.

6 They killed Shekhem and Hamor and recovered Dinah from the house.

7 The other sons entered afterward and took the city's possessions because their sister had been dishonored.

8 Yaakov feared the surrounding peoples because his household was few in number.

9 A terror from YHWH fell upon the neighboring cities so that they did not pursue Yaakov's sons.

10 The deed concerning Dinah was recorded as a warning against giving daughters of Yisra'EL to men of foreign nations.

11 The heavenly tablets prohibit such intermarriage because it brings defilement into the covenant people.

12 A man who gives his daughter to a foreigner for marriage is charged with a grave covenant offense.

13 The same judgment concerns one who takes a foreign woman in a way that abandons the covenant boundary.

14 Yisra'EL is commanded to separate itself from the impurity of the nations and not imitate their practices.

15 Failure to confront such defilement brings judgment upon the community that tolerates it.

16 No offering can conceal deliberate covenant pollution while the offense is being protected.

17 Moshe is commanded to testify to Yisra'EL about what happened at Shekhem as a warning for later generations.

18 Shim'on and Levi's action against the men of Shekhem was remembered within Yovelim as judgment for Dinah's violation.

19 Levi was chosen for priestly service because of his zeal in the matter and his devotion to the covenant boundary.

20 The priestly line was assigned to Levi and his descendants to approach before YHWH and serve in the sanctuary.

21 The chapter links purity of family unions with the holiness required of the sanctuary and priesthood.

22 Yisra'EL is warned that covenant holiness cannot be preserved while foreign cultic practices are welcomed into the household.

23 The heavenly record treats sexual violence and covenant betrayal as matters requiring judgment, not concealment.

24 The command is directed to both men and women within Yisra'EL and is framed as a continuing ordinance.

25 The memory of Dinah therefore becomes both a judgment narrative and a legal warning for the generations.

26 These statutes concerning marriage, defilement, and Levi's selection are given to Moshe as part of Yovelim's covenant testimony.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] MT Genesis 34 supplies the Dinah-Shekhem narrative. Jubilees expands the episode into explicit anti-intermarriage legislation and Levi-related priestly interpretation beyond the narrative form preserved in the MT.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Chapter 30 deliberately joins the Dinah narrative to an extended intermarriage law. The legal section is not an editorial appendix to be separated from the story; in Jubilees the narrative functions as the precedent for the legislation.

YOVELIM — CHAPTER 31 Purification and Bethel — Yitzhak Blesses Levi and Yehudah

1 At the new moon Yaakov told everyone in his household to purify themselves, change their garments, put away the foreign deities among them, and go with him to Bethel, where he had made his vow when fleeing from Esav.

2 They gave Yaakov the foreign objects and ornaments they possessed, including the household images Rachel had taken from Lavan; Yaakov broke and destroyed them and hid the remains beneath an oak near Shekhem.

3 Yaakov went up to Bethel on the new moon of the seventh month.

4 He built an altar at the place where he had slept, set up a pillar, and sent word inviting his father Yitzhak and his mother Rivkah to come to the sacrifice.

5 Yitzhak asked that Yaakov come to him so he could see his son before he died.

6 Yaakov went to Yitzhak and Rivkah at the house associated with Avraham, taking Levi and Yehudah with him.

7 Rivkah came out to embrace and kiss Yaakov; when she saw Levi and Yehudah she embraced and blessed them, declaring that Avraham's seed would become renowned through them and be a blessing on the earth.

8 Yaakov entered the room where Yitzhak lay, took his father's hand, bent down, and kissed him; Yitzhak embraced Yaakov and wept upon his neck.

9 Yitzhak's sight cleared and he saw Levi and Yehudah, recognizing their likeness to Yaakov.

10 Yaakov confirmed that they were truly his sons.

11 The two sons approached Yitzhak, and he kissed and embraced them together.

12 The spirit of prophecy came upon Yitzhak, and he took Levi with his right hand and Yehudah with his left.

13 Yitzhak blessed Levi first, asking the Creator of all ages to bless Levi and his descendants through every age.

14 He asked that Levi and his descendants be raised from among all flesh to approach and serve in the sanctuary, corresponding to the angels of the presence and the holy ones.

15 He declared that Levi's descendants would be princes, judges, and leaders among Yaakov's sons, speaking YHWH's word and judging his judgments in righteousness.

16 He said Levi's name was rightly given: Levi would be joined to YHWH and remain among Yaakov's sons; the sacred table would belong to him and his descendants, and their provision would not fail.

17 Yitzhak pronounced that Levi's adversaries would fall, those who blessed him would be blessed, and those who cursed him would be cursed.

18 Then Yitzhak blessed Yehudah, asking YHWH to give him strength and power over those who hated him and declaring that a ruler from his line would stand over Yaakov's sons.

19 He said Yehudah's name and the name of his descendants would spread through lands and regions, and nations would fear before them.

20 Yitzhak declared that help for Yaakov and deliverance for Yisra'EL would be found in Yehudah.

21 He said that when Yehudah sat upon the throne of righteous honor, great peace would come to the seed of the beloved; those who blessed him would be blessed, while those who hated, afflicted, or cursed him would be uprooted.

22 Yitzhak kissed and embraced Yehudah again and rejoiced because he had truly seen the sons of Yaakov.

23 Yaakov bowed before his father, and Yitzhak blessed them; Yaakov remained with Yitzhak that night, and they ate and drank with joy.

24 Yitzhak placed Levi and Yehudah to sleep, one at his right hand and one at his left, and it was counted to him as righteousness.

25 During the night Yaakov told Yitzhak how YHWH had shown him mercy, prospered his journey, and guarded him from evil; Yitzhak blessed the Creator of Avraham for preserving mercy toward his descendants.

26 In the morning Yaakov told Yitzhak about his vow, the vision he had seen, the altar he had built, and the sacrifice prepared for fulfillment of the vow, and he had come intending to take his father with him.

27 Yitzhak said he was too old to endure the journey and told Yaakov to go in peace, taking Rivkah with him if she went.

28 Yitzhak gave thanks that he and Yaakov had lived to see one another again and blessed the day of their meeting.

29 He urged Yaakov to fulfill his vow without delay, because a person is accountable for a vow made to YHWH.

30 Yitzhak told Rivkah to go with Yaakov; Rivkah and her nurse Devorah accompanied him to Bethel.

31 Yaakov remembered Yitzhak's blessing over him, Levi, and Yehudah, rejoiced, and blessed the Creator of his fathers Avraham and Yitzhak.

32 Yaakov declared that he now knew he and his sons possessed enduring hope before YHWH; the blessings of Yitzhak over Levi and Yehudah were recorded as an enduring testimony on the heavenly tablets.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Chapter 31 expands the Bethel-family material with blessings associated especially with Levi and Yehudah. These blessing units are textually important additions to Yovelim and should not be collapsed into the shorter Genesis return-to-Bethel narrative.

YOVELIM — CHAPTER 32 Levi's Priesthood — Tithes — Bethel Vision — Binyamin and Rachel

1 That night at Bethel, Levi dreamed that he and his sons had been appointed priests of the Most High for all generations; he awoke and blessed YHWH.

2 Early on the fourteenth day Yaakov gave a tenth of everything that had come with him, including people, livestock, gold, vessels, and garments.

3 During those days Rachel was pregnant with Binyamin; when Yaakov counted his sons in reverse order, Levi fell as the tenth, and Yaakov clothed him in priestly garments and installed him for service.

4 On the fifteenth day Yaakov brought a large offering from the cattle, rams, sheep, lambs, and goats as a burnt offering before YHWH.

5 This offering fulfilled the vow by which Yaakov had promised to give a tenth, together with the accompanying offerings and libations.

6 After the fire consumed the burnt offering, Yaakov offered incense and thank offerings, and he continued making festival offerings each day for seven days.

7 Yaakov, his sons, and his people ate with joy throughout the seven days, blessing and thanking YHWH for delivering him from all his troubles and allowing him to fulfill his vow.

8 Yaakov tithed all clean animals and offered the holy portion, while the unclean animals were not assigned to Levi; the persons belonging to the household were also counted in the tithe arrangement.

9 Levi performed priestly service at Bethel before Yaakov, taking precedence over his brothers; through Levi, Yaakov set apart again the tithe as holy to YHWH.

10 Because of this, the heavenly tablets record a continuing law concerning the tithe of the tithe to be eaten before YHWH at the place chosen for his name.

11 The ordinance is to be fulfilled year by year, and the second tithe is not to be carried over from one year into the next.

12 The produce is to be eaten within its year, each according to its appointed season.

13 Anything left until it becomes old is treated as polluted and is to be burned rather than retained.

14 The holy portion is to be eaten together at the sanctuary and not allowed to become old.

15 The tithes of cattle and sheep are holy to YHWH and belong to the priests, who eat them before him from year to year, as written on the heavenly tablets.

16 On the following night, the twenty-second day of the month, Yaakov resolved to build up the place, surround its court, and sanctify it permanently for himself and his descendants.

17 YHWH appeared to him by night, blessed him, and declared that he would no longer be called only Yaakov but would be named Yisra'EL.

18 The Creator of heaven and earth promised to increase Yaakov greatly and said kings would come from him and exercise judgment wherever humanity lived.

19 He promised Yaakov's descendants the earth under heaven and said that they would ultimately inherit it.

20 When the revelation ended, Yaakov watched as the divine presence ascended from him.

21 Yaakov then saw in a night vision an angel descend from heaven holding seven tablets; the angel gave them to Yaakov, who read what was written concerning what would happen to him and his sons through the ages.

22 The angel showed him the contents and warned him not to make Bethel the permanent sanctuary or settle there, but to return to the house of Avraham and live with Yitzhak until his father's death.

23 The angel told Yaakov that he would die in Mitzrayim in peace but would be buried with honor in the land of his fathers beside Avraham and Yitzhak.

24 Yaakov was told not to fear: what he had seen and read would occur, and he was to write it all down.

25 When Yaakov asked how he could remember everything he had read and seen, the angel promised to bring it all back to his memory.

26 Yaakov awoke remembering the vision and wrote down all the words he had read and seen.

27 He celebrated an additional eighth day and sacrificed on it as on the preceding days, distinguishing this added day from the seven-day feast.

28 The heavenly tablets record this added day with the feast, establishing the complete festival observance revealed to Yaakov.

29 The added day was entered among the appointed festival days within the reckoning of the year.

30 On the night of the twenty-third, Devorah, Rivkah's nurse, died; they buried her beneath the city under an oak and named the place in memory of her mourning.

31 Rivkah returned to Yitzhak, and Yaakov sent livestock with her so she could prepare for his father the food he desired.

32 Yaakov followed his mother as far as the land of Kabratan and stayed there.

33 Rachel gave birth during the night; because of her suffering she named the child Son of My Sorrow, but Yaakov named him Binyamin.

34 Rachel died and was buried in the land of Ephrath, that is Bethlehem, and Yaakov erected a pillar over her grave beside the road.

[DSS] 4Q223–224 (4QpapJubʰ) preserves 32:18–21 (DJD XIII, 95–140). Only surviving/readable material at the stated locus is treated as manuscript evidence; brackets, restored lacunae, and editorial retroversion are not treated as physically preserved Hebrew.

This reader does not claim a new diplomatic transcription of every individual Geʽez codex; Qumran Hebrew is applied only at extant loci.

YOVELIM — CHAPTER 50 Jubilees and Sabbath Laws

1 After the Passover law, Moshe is told that the Sabbath days in the wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai, had also been made known to him.

2 At Mount Sinai he had been instructed about the Sabbaths of the land and the jubilee years within the cycles of sabbatical years, although the specific jubilee year was not to be fully identified until Yisra'EL entered the land it would possess.

3 The land itself is to observe its Sabbaths while the people dwell upon it, and through those cycles they are to know the jubilee year.

4 The weeks of years and jubilees are arranged from Adam to Moshe's time as forty-nine jubilees plus one week and two years. Forty additional years remain for learning YHWH's commandments before the crossing into Kena'an westward over the Yarden.

5 The jubilees will continue until Yisra'EL is purified from sexual wrongdoing, impurity, contamination, sin, and error and can dwell securely throughout the land. The passage anticipates a time with no satan or evil one and with the land remaining pure.

6 The Sabbath commandments and the statutes governing the Sabbath are then written down for Moshe.

7 Work is permitted for six days, but the seventh is the Sabbath of YHWH. No work is to be done on it by the people, their children, male or female servants, their animals, or the foreigner residing among them.

8 A person who performs prohibited work on the Sabbath is subject to death. The prohibition includes desecrating the day, sexual relations, planning ordinary work or a journey, conducting buying or selling, drawing water not prepared on the sixth day, or carrying a load outside one's tent or house.

9 Nothing needed for the Sabbath is to be prepared on that day if it could have been prepared on the sixth day. Food and drink are to be ready beforehand so that the day can be spent eating, drinking, resting from work, keeping Sabbath, and blessing YHWH. The day is designated as a holy festival and as a day of holy kingship for Yisra'EL throughout its generations.

10 Yisra'EL is given the honor of eating, drinking, being satisfied, and resting on the Sabbath. Ordinary human labor is excluded, while sanctuary service involving incense, offerings, and sacrifices appointed for the days and Sabbaths is excepted.

11 Only that sanctuary service is to be performed on Sabbath days in the sanctuary of YHWH, so that continual offerings may make atonement for Yisra'EL and stand as an acceptable memorial before YHWH day by day.

12 The prohibited acts are expanded: ordinary work, travel, agricultural labor at home or elsewhere, kindling fire, riding an animal, sea travel by ship, striking or killing, slaughtering an animal or bird, capturing a wild animal, bird, or fish, fasting, and making war on the Sabbath.

13 Anyone who deliberately performs these prohibited acts on the Sabbath is subject to death. The children of Yisra'EL are therefore to keep the Sabbaths according to the commandments for the Sabbaths of the land, as written on the tablets entrusted to the angel so that the laws of the appointed times and their divisions could be written for Moshe. With this, the account of the divisions of the times is completed.
